result.title: Efficient Conformal Calibration for Paired Recommendation Decisions
result.summary: Risk control can suppress useful changes to a frozen recommendation rule. We study how to recover valid activation from the same observed fractional losses. Two specified internal calibrators can lose efficiency by compressing losses into their sum or clipping auxiliary inverse counts before averaging. We propose Averaged Conformal Risk Calibration, or ACRC, which averages before clipping. A product identity proves expected-risk validity, while pointwise bounds characterize the additional activation. For fixed populations sampled without replacement, we connect activation to signed utility under heterogeneous users and switching constraints. Near the budgets, positive population mean gain and the stated nondegeneracy conditions give positive leading-order utility increments despite sampling dependence. Across six datasets, changing only calibration improves discounted net utility by $0.010226$ over raw and $0.008337$ over RB. A separately frozen Jester confirmation gives $0.011025 \pm 0.001082$ over raw with the rule and filter fixed, using a five-seed approximate 95 percent paired interval. Against information-matched SCoRE selecting risk or reward scores, the mean utility difference is $+0.015934 \pm 0.001440$. These gains use more mean realized risk within the declared budgets. Upstream failures delimit the benefit: efficient calibration releases useful modifications when the proposals themselves have value.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在冻结推荐规则下如何从观测分数损失中恢复有效的激活决策，提出 ACRC：先平均再裁剪的 conformal 风险校准，并给出期望风险有效性的乘积恒等式与逐点激活界，在六个数据集及 Jester 上验证净效用提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其在给定风险预算下判定「是否激活改动」并给出有效性保证的校准方式，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的阈值校准与预算约束提供方法线索；但原文限于推荐决策，迁移可行性需核查。
